stories.head: Astra's bold AI gamble could backfire
stories.body: Astra's CEO Chris Kemp is betting heavily on AI to save the company, which once soared on SPAC hype but is now struggling. While he claims he might be the last one standing, investors might wonder if this is a strategic pivot or a desperate move. With revenue still elusive, the stakes are high for a company that needs more than just algorithms to stay afloat.
stories.soWhat: When a CEO starts talking about being the last one standing, it’s usually a sign of trouble—especially if AI is the lifeline.

stories.head: Japan's H3 rocket comeback is reassuring
stories.body: Japan's H3 rocket successfully launched six smallsats, marking a significant recovery after its previous failure. This launch is crucial for Japan's space ambitions and demonstrates that persistence can lead to success—even in aerospace. As the global competition heats up, a reliable launch vehicle can make all the difference for national pride and economic investment.
stories.soWhat: In an industry where failures are common, Japan's ability to bounce back with H3 could provide a blueprint for others navigating their own launch woes.

stories.head: AAC Clyde Space nets €10.9M ESA contract
stories.body: AAC Clyde Space has secured a €10.9 million contract from the European Space Agency to enhance its maritime monitoring capabilities. This contract underscores the ongoing demand for satellite-based solutions in environmental monitoring and security. With the ESA's focus on sustainability, this deal positions AAC Clyde Space favorably in a competitive market.
stories.soWhat: Contracts like this are the real currency in the space sector; they not only validate a company's technology but also its market relevance.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
